accuracy.evidence: Checked against Common Core ELA SL.5.5 ('Include multimedia components (e.g., graphics, sound) and visual displays in presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes') and SL.4.5, and the National Curriculum in England KS2 spoken language statements (give well-structured descriptions, explanations and presentations; gain, maintain and monitor the interest of the listener(s)). The guidance on slides follows Mayer's multimedia learning principles (coherence: cut extraneous pictures, sounds and words; redundancy: do not put the spoken script as on-screen text; temporal contiguity: show the picture while the words are spoken; signalling: titles and labels) and W3C WCAG 2.1 guidance that pre-recorded video with speech needs captions (1.2.2). The talk is fictional, so its numbers (4 m in 2023, 2 m in 2025) are internally consistent: 2 m is half of 4 m.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented habits of novice presenters (Mayer 2009 coherence and redundancy effects; NCTE/ReadWriteThink and Oracy Cambridge presentation guidance): decorative images that show no point (the cat in step 1 and the puppy in the challenge, tag pretty, m4), copying the script onto slides and reading it (step 2 prediction, tags script and read, m8), animation and background music (step 3, tags flash and music, m2), mismatching media and information (step 4 with a reason for every wrong choice, tags pic, chart and clip), showing visuals at the wrong moment (step 5, tags early and late), and fixing hearing access by volume instead of captions (tags loud and skip, m6).

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed (under 30% similar to every flagship lab). 950 Text & Media Connections (flagscreen) compares a story with its film or audiobook; 812 Interpreting visual information reads visuals in texts; 470 Choosing Form and Tone is about written register. This lab is about building a presentation: dragging a visual onto each spoken point, striking script text off a slide, removing distracting extras from a slide, choosing media for kinds of information, and switching slides in step with a script.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers each rule by doing: the cat card fits no point and is refused with the reason; the slide's word count drops from 49 to 11 as script chunks are struck, while cutting the title or the key numbers is refused; removing the chart or its labels is refused because they carry the idea, while the star, cat and music go; each wrong media choice explains why it cannot show that kind of information; choosing a slide ahead of or behind Sam's line is refused as 'for a later point' or 'for an earlier point'.

predictions.evidence: Step 1: 'Which visual makes it clearest?' with a cute frog photo and the typed sentence tempting; the chart is the only visual that fits the shrinking point. Step 2: 'Which slide helps listeners follow Sam best?' with 'Every word Sam will say' and 'no words at all' tempting; the cut slide keeps only the title and the key numbers.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Every distractor in the eight challenge questions has its own tag and WHY message in deck_art.js (pic, script, flash, loud, skip, early, late, music, chart, clip, pretty, read, small). In the lab, each wrong placement, cut, removal, media choice and slide choice gives a message naming that slip.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons readability check passes (learner kid ≤ 6.5, adult ≤ 9.5). Kid sentences are short ('A slide is not your script.'), and the precise terms for the band (multimedia, visual display, slide, chart, caption, main point, key words) are explained where they first appear.

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler phrases. The four kid paragraphs match the visual-for-a-point, media-type, key-words and distraction/timing ideas; the adult text gives the standards, what each task does and the named mistakes; every hint points to a question the learner can ask (which point does it help? what kind of information is it?).

mobile.evidence: Screenshots of every step at start and after Show me at 360 px (Android, 2x) in dark theme, checked by eye: point rows, slide text and media tiles fit without clipping; tiles fall to 2 columns on narrow screens; thumbnails stay at least 50 px wide; every action also has a full-width button below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: gate_browser passed: axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13, all 5 tasks complete with Show me, the challenge shows, no console errors. Every canvas action has a button (Point n: visual, Cut '…', Remove the …, the five media, Show the … slide), drag has a tap-then-tap fallback, and the canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action.
